title: Review repair H: a merge refusal must not destroy the report, and a passing check must not be reused at a new commit
description:
Two blockers from the qeu final review (gcx), both verified against the tree at the wave 10 merge.

(1) A merge refusal destroys the only copy of the report.
internal/reconcile/dispatch.go:181 calls disposeRefused for EVERY refusal integrate returns, which is the RefusedMerge set in integrate.go (lines 49, 52, 55, 99, 125, 149). disposeRejected -> tearDown removes the worktree, and the report lives INSIDE the worktree (internal/exec/subprocess/state.go:60-63: ResultPath is absolute and inside the attempt worktree). integrate never sets the tick to rejected, so on the next run disposition() takes the adopt path, integratedHead is empty (nothing was merged), and collect runs again against a worktree that is gone. The tick comes back as collect_failed: missing-result, permanently, and the real verdict (the merge conflict) is lost.
Note: 0c1 deliberately widened teardown to every refusal class. The fix is NOT to revert that. The fix is that a refusal whose attempt will be COLLECTED AGAIN must keep what the next collect reads.

(2) The gate rekey reuses a PASS across commits.
internal/reconcile/gate.go:372: gateEvidenceKey returns the plain key when the existing record's Result is "pass", so only a FAILING check is rekeyed by gateSHA. With a multi-command gate, a check that passed at commit A is reused at commit B while the run publishes the whole verdict under B's fingerprint and closes the tick. A pass at A is not evidence about B. The doc comment above it (gate.go:353-359) claims a record "is keyed to the commit it ran on", which is true only for failures.

Both are in the wave 9/10 repair surface, so they are in scope for this epic rather than the backlog.

Full findings, with failure scenarios, at:
/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-peterengelbrecht-Development-ticfac/1687f85b-9680-4c8b-ad98-ebe61eb3bfb3/scratchpad/review/wave910-findings.md

Also fix these three should-fix items from the same review; they are the same surface:
- internal/exec/subprocess/cancel.go:61 hasSettled calls a still-RUNNING attempt settled, because observe returns succeeded from the report before it checks liveness. Cancel then writes no durable refusal and returns StopRequested false after stopTree already killed the process tree.
- internal/reconcile/dispatch.go:549 integratedHead swallows a remote-read error and answers "not merged", the opposite of the rule disposition states just above it. An unreachable remote must be an operational error, never a verdict.
- internal/reconcile/settle.go:222 rejectedDurably lets an operator release a gate-failed attempt whose work is ALREADY MERGED, which contradicts the file's own prose and strands the tick in a redispatch loop.

Leave these two OUT of this tick, they are routed separately: the rekey firing on every resume because GateSHA comes from the live epic head; and disposition keying off tick state without the attempt number. Do not widen scope beyond the six items above.

Rules: read .tick/config.md and .tick/learnings.md fresh from your worktree. contracts/ is vendored and digest-pinned, never hand-edit it; an upstream contract problem goes in your RESULT file as an UPSTREAM ticks FINDING for the orchestrator to file. Go stdlib-first.

Report: write RESULT-<your-tick-id>.md in your worktree root, ending with a line "STATUS: DONE" or "STATUS: BLOCKED".

acceptance_criteria: A merge refusal keeps what the next collect reads: a test drives a conflicting attempt through integrate, asserts the refusal, and asserts the next run reports the MERGE refusal (not collect_failed: missing-result) — either by keeping the worktree for a re-collectable refusal or by marking the tick rejected so disposition stops re-collecting; the choice is logged in the RESULT file with its reasoning. A passing check is re-run when the commit changes: a test with a multi-command gate asserts that a check which passed at commit A is not reused as evidence at commit B, and gate.go's doc comment says what the code actually does. cancel.go hasSettled checks liveness before it trusts a report's success. integratedHead returns an operational error rather than "not merged" when the remote cannot be read. rejectedDurably refuses to release an attempt whose work is already merged. go test -short -timeout 45m ./... green (make test-short).
